name: New Orleans
tagline: 25-cent martinis at a 19th-century classic, and beignets worth the line every time.

Commander's Palace.description: Creole and Cajun cuisine since the 19th century, winner of seven James Beard awards. The 25-cent martini lunch is a local ritual. Critic Ian McNulty (Times-Picayune / NOLA.com) wrote: "Nobody makes fine dining more fun than Commander's."

Café du Monde.description: Beignets and chicory coffee at the French Market since the 19th century, with a constant line and zero pretension.

Galatoire's.description: French Creole cuisine on Bourbon Street since 1905, now run by the fourth generation of the Galatoire family.

Dooky Chase's Restaurant.description: Creole cooking since 1941 and a historic meeting point of the Civil Rights Movement, with Martin Luther King Jr. among its visitors.

Domilise's Po-Boy & Bar.description: A no-frills family-run po-boy shop since 1918. Anthony Bourdain ordered the off-menu special (fried shrimp, Swiss cheese, and roast beef gravy) on "No Reservations" (2008) and said he'd have a serious problem if he lived nearby. Holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand distinction.
